titleEn: In the Dark, Jingle the Bell!

pages.text: "Tonight we all sleep in the attic!" Lulu spread a blanket. Three cousins tumbled in, giggling. The wooden shutters were already shut tight.
Mom came upstairs with a little lamp. "Sleep well." She blew it out. All dark! Winter wind whistled beyond the shutters. Lulu pulled the blanket to the nose.
Something pointed stood against the wall. Two horns! "I want to sleep too... What is that?" Lulu's ears stood up, body shivering. The cousins were already sleeping softly.
Lulu gripped the neck bell and jingled it. Footsteps climbed the stairs. "Mom is here, Lulu." She held Lulu's hand tightly.
"What scared you?" Lulu pointed a forepaw at the wall. "Something with horns..." Mom nodded. "You were scared. Shall we look one by one?"
Mom lit the lamp and shone it on the wall. The horns were a bundle of dried olive branches hanging there. "Oh? Branches?" Lulu's mouth rounded.
Now Lulu held the lamp in both forepaws and lit the corner. A folded blanket! That long thing by the door—a broom! "In the dark, jingle the bell!"
Lulu blew out the lamp. Dark again, but only branches, a blanket, and a broom were there. In the dark remained Lulu's two eyes and blue bell.
Under the blanket, Lulu counted three blunt fingers. "One, say you are scared! Two, jingle the bell! Three, hold your cousin's hand!" Lulu held a sleeping cousin's hand.
Mom tucked the blanket to Lulu's chin and patted the back. Being able to call makes darkness less scary. "When the bell rings, Mom comes." "In the dark, jingle the bell!" Lulu's eyes closed.
